options: A specific type named T defined elsewhere
A placeholder for a type, chosen when the function is called
A variable holding a runtime value
quiz.explain: T is a generic type parameter — a placeholder. The compiler fills it with a concrete type each time you call the function.

quiz.q: Why does a generic function often need a trait bound like `<T: PartialOrd>`?
options: To make the code run faster at runtime
Because T could be any type, so you may only use abilities you promise it has
Bounds are optional decoration with no effect
To turn the generic into a trait object
quiz.explain: Inside a generic, T might be anything, so the compiler only allows operations you guarantee via bounds. `PartialOrd` promises T can be compared with `>`.

quiz.q: What does the `+` mean in `<T: PartialOrd + Copy>`?
options: T is either PartialOrd or Copy
Add PartialOrd and Copy together numerically
T must implement both PartialOrd and Copy
quiz.explain: The `+` combines bounds: T must satisfy PartialOrd AND Copy.

options: They are free to type on the keyboard
The compiler generates specialized code per concrete type, so there's no runtime penalty
They use a garbage collector to manage memory
quiz.explain: For each concrete type used, the compiler stamps out a specialized version (monomorphization), so generic code runs as fast as hand-written specific code.

flashcards.front: What is a generic type parameter like T?
flashcards.back: A placeholder for a type, chosen when the code is used. Declared in angle brackets: fn name<T>(...) or struct Name<T>.

flashcards.front: Why do you add trait bounds to a generic?
flashcards.back: Inside a generic, T could be any type, so you may only use abilities you promise it has. Bounds like <T: PartialOrd> grant those abilities.
T must implement both PartialOrd (comparable) and Copy (cheaply duplicated). The + means 'and also'.

flashcards.front: Do generics slow down your program?
flashcards.back: No — they are zero-cost. The compiler generates a specialized version per concrete type, so runtime speed matches hand-written code.
